reviewer: ECO-01 maker — not an independent accuracy approval

claims.publicWording: Generative AI can produce false content and fabricated citations, so important sources and citations still need review and verification.
claims.supportLocation: NIST.AI.600-1, pp. 9 and 34: confabulation includes confidently false content and fabricated citations; suggested actions require review and verification of sources and citations.
claims.scope: Generative-AI risk management; not a performance rate or guarantee for a named model.
claims.qualification: Sourced fact, scoped to the NIST risk profile.

claims.publicWording: Current AI products can search the web and present citations; those are present capabilities, not hypothetical future abilities.
claims.supportLocation: Web search guide, Web search and Output and citations sections: web search can access up-to-date information and responses include inline URL citation annotations.
claims.scope: OpenAI API web-search tool; availability and implementation depend on current provider documentation.
claims.qualification: Provider documentation establishes the provider-described capability, not comparative accuracy.

history.change: Reopened the current official web-search guide before release; capability, citation behavior, scope and qualification remain supported.

claims.publicWording: Search grounding can connect generated answers to current web material and return citation annotations.
claims.supportLocation: Grounding with Google Search, How grounding with Google Search works and Understanding the grounding response: real-time web content, grounded response and inline URL citation annotations.
claims.publicationVersion: Current web documentation · page updated 2026-07-30 UTC
claims.scope: Gemini API grounding feature; does not establish source quality, entailment or universal truth.
claims.qualification: Provider documentation establishes the provider-described operation only.

history.change: Reopened the official page after its 2026-07-30 update; current google_search workflow and inline citation annotations still support the bounded claim.

claims.publicWording: Grounding, direct quotations, citations and permission to express uncertainty can reduce hallucination risk, but they do not eliminate it; critical information still needs validation.
claims.supportLocation: Reduce hallucinations, Basic hallucination minimization strategies and closing limitation: allow uncertainty, use direct quotes, verify with citations, and always validate critical information.
claims.scope: Risk-reduction guidance, not comparative model evidence or a guarantee.
claims.qualification: Provider guidance plus its explicit limitation.

history.change: Reopened the current official guidance; the named techniques and explicit critical-information limitation remain present.

claims.publicWording: A citation is a pointer to a source; verification additionally checks the source’s identity, relevance, scope, date and support for the specific claim.
claims.supportLocation: NIST pp. 9 and 34 require source/citation review; COR About names source identity, evidence and other-source questions. The five-part formulation is LAiDIES’ synthesis.
claims.publicationVersion: NIST AI 600-1; current COR About page
claims.scope: Instructional verification model, not a universal legal standard.
claims.qualification: Qualified LAiDIES synthesis; not attributed verbatim to either source.

claims.publicWording: Lateral reading means leaving an unfamiliar page to investigate who is behind it and what trusted sources say about it.
claims.supportLocation: Intro to Lateral Reading, opening lesson description: defines the strategy as leaving the webpage and opening a new tab to see what trusted websites say about the unknown source.
claims.scope: Evaluating unfamiliar online sources; it is one verification action, not the entire Receipt Loop.
claims.qualification: Directly supported by the named Digital Inquiry Group lesson.

history.change: Replaced non-entailing COR About attribution with the entailing Intro to Lateral Reading lesson after independent review.

claims.publicWording: C2PA provenance can bind claims about an asset’s source and history so tampering can be detected; it does not decide whether the content or provenance is good, bad or true.
claims.supportLocation: C2PA 2.4 Content Credentials specification §§1.2 Scope, 1.3 Technical Overview and 2.3 Core Aspects; the trust model provides tamper-evident provenance and does not make value judgments.
claims.scope: C2PA-compatible Content Credentials; not every metadata or authenticity system.
claims.qualification: Provenance and tamper evidence are not a truth score.

history.change: Superseded C2PA 2.2 with current 2.4 after the version trigger fired; teaching distinction retained and support locations rebound.

claims.publicWording: At 320 CSS pixels, the rendered candidate must reflow without loss of information or functionality and without two-dimensional scrolling except where an exception applies.
claims.scope: Rendered web reader acceptance; conformance requires more than this single criterion.
claims.qualification: Acceptance requirement, not a claim that this candidate already conforms.
claims.nextReview: On W3C errata or Recommendation change

claims.publicWording: The Receipt Loop uses four evidence verdicts: supported, contradicted, unresolved and not applicable.
claims.supportLocation: ECO-01 build packet, correct mental model and chapter 5.
claims.scope: LAiDIES teaching taxonomy, not a claim that every external framework uses these labels.

claims.publicWording: Checking effort should be proportional to consequence, reversibility, uncertainty and freshness.
claims.supportLocation: ECO-01 build packet, Stakes dial and proportionality contract.
claims.scope: General verification triage; does not replace professional standards or regulated duties.
claims.qualification: Internal instructional recommendation pending newcomer evidence.

claims.publicWording: Separate URLs are not independent corroboration when they all trace to the same underlying source.
claims.supportLocation: COR asks what other sources say and teaches leaving a page to investigate an unknown source; the origin-tracing formulation is LAiDIES’ synthesis.
claims.scope: Evidence independence; distinct reporting may still add independent analysis.
claims.qualification: Qualified synthesis, not a direct quotation or universal rule.

claims.publicWording: The source-bound prompt is a risk-reduction aid, not a truth machine, and critical claims still require external validation.
claims.supportLocation: Reduce hallucinations, closing limitation: the techniques significantly reduce hallucinations but do not eliminate them; critical information must still be validated.
claims.scope: Prompt use with generative AI; no prompt can certify arbitrary sources or conclusions.
claims.qualification: Safety limit retained next to the prompt.

history.change: Reopened the current official guidance; its non-elimination and critical-validation warning continues to support this limitation.

claims.publicWording: The Rulebook is not legal, medical, financial, HR or safety advice and cannot replace the responsible professional or decision owner.
claims.supportLocation: ECO-01 build packet, stakes dial and safety acceptance test.
claims.nextReview: Every release and on safety incident

claims.publicWording: A real source can accurately describe an old state and still be inapplicable to a current decision.
claims.supportLocation: ECO-01 build packet, misconception correction and freshness contract.
claims.scope: Distinguishes historical accuracy from present applicability.
